title: Plaque and Bleeding on Probing Around Implants Supporting Fixed Full-Arch Dental Prostheses
official: Time Since Prosthesis Removal or Installation and Peri-Implant Clinical Findings in Patients With Implant-Supported Fixed Full-Arch Prostheses: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study
summary: This observational study examines plaque, hard deposits (calculus), and gum bleeding around dental implants supporting fixed full-arch dental prostheses. The main question is whether the time since the prosthesis was last removed or installed is associated with bleeding around the implants. The study also examines associations with plaque, calculus, smoking, diabetes, and use of a water flosser. Participants undergo no treatment assigned by a research protocol. The study combines a single clinical assessment with information from existing dental records. Clinical data from 43 patients with 279 implants are available; eight additional patients identified in the source registry lack clinical measurements and are included only in the selection flow. Associations do not establish that a longer interval causes inflammation.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients previously rehabilitated with an implant-supported full-arch fixed dental prosthesis (Toronto Bridge) in the maxilla, mandible, or both arches.
* Patients included in the clinical registry of the participating dental practice.
* Availability of clinical records documenting the implant-supported rehabilitation and relevant treatment history.
* Written informed consent for the use of clinical data for research purposes.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients without a history of implant-supported full-arch fixed prosthetic rehabilitation.
* Patients without sufficient clinical documentation to establish their eligibility.
* Patients who did not provide informed consent for the use of their clinical data.
